segments.title: Testing Battlestar Deadlock with naval design lessons
segments.summary: Battlestar Galactica Deadlock's warships provide a fictional test case for lessons from naval history and current warship design.
segments.body: The game offers a compact way to ask familiar naval questions about armament, protection, aircraft, and fleet roles. Its fictional battles are a design exercise rather than a reproduction of historical combat. The test is whether the spacecraft layouts make sense beside the accumulated experience of real navies and current warship practice. This opening establishes the historical basis for the later criticisms of firing arcs, carrier capacity, and fleet balance.

evidence.note: He introduces the game and says he will consider lessons from naval history and current warship design.

segments.title: Manticore corvettes: useful mass, weak firing arcs
segments.summary: The inexpensive Manticore corvette works as a missile-firing base of fire, but its fore-and-aft guns leave dangerous blind areas.
segments.body: Massing Manticores creates a simple, inexpensive base of fire with a useful missile system. Their low cost makes them a plausible general-purpose unit for a fictional space navy. The problem is geometric: fore-and-aft guns invite an opponent to attack from the beam, where maneuverability and missile capacity cannot make up for a missing gun arc. Top-and-bottom mounts or weapons able to cover a full circle would use a spacecraft's three-dimensional form more effectively.

evidence.note: He praises the Manticore's low cost and missile system, then criticizes its fore-and-aft gun coverage.

segments.title: Real warship gunnery aims for all-round coverage
segments.summary: The Adamant's side-mounted guns prompt a comparison with destroyers designed to keep useful firing arcs across much more of the horizon.
segments.body: A spacecraft can use top-and-bottom mounts or careful weapon placement to cover more approaches than a conventional hull. The game's blind zones contrast with Tribal-class destroyers, whose fore-and-aft guns retained useful arcs toward the opposite end of the ship, and Battle-class destroyers, whose forward concentration cleared their fields of fire. Real designers and naval officers generally resisted leaving a large sector entirely uncovered. The omission seems especially implausible for an advanced society that has used these designs long enough for service experience to reveal their blind arcs. Some Colonial ships also ask the same guns to serve as both the main armament and the close-in defensive system, although those roles require different coverage and responsiveness.

evidence.note: He discusses Adamant gun placement and compares it with the firing arcs of Tribal- and Battle-class destroyers.

segments.title: The Ranger cruiser as a fragile missile platform
segments.summary: The Ranger carries a useful missile load, but it is too vulnerable to serve comfortably as a close-action cruiser.
segments.body: The Ranger works best high and outside enemy gun range, making broad, lazy turns while it launches missiles. Its double missile load is useful against major Cylon units, but the hull is too lightly protected for close action. Once the missiles are exhausted, it can move in after Manticores and other ships have reduced the dangerous targets. Despite its cruiser label, the Ranger functions as a standoff contributor sheltered by tougher units.

evidence.note: He describes keeping Ranger cruisers outside gun range and relying on their missiles because they feel vulnerable.

segments.title: Why a larger battlestar should carry more aircraft
segments.summary: Giving the Artemis and the larger Jupiter battlestar the same air group wastes an obvious advantage of the bigger ship.
segments.body: Aircraft capacity should be a central reason to build a larger capital ship. Giving the Artemis and the larger Jupiter the same number of squadrons therefore wastes a force-design opportunity. These spacecraft do not have to fit through the Suez or Panama canals, although construction capacity still limits their size. If the setting can support a larger hull and external launch-and-recovery pods, the Jupiter should gain substantially more hangar space instead of duplicating the Artemis air group.

evidence.note: He questions why Artemis and Jupiter battlestars carry the same air group and argues for expanded hangar space.

segments.title: Standoff missiles meet a fighter-heavy battlespace
segments.summary: Long-range missile combat may suit space, but the game's confined engagements and important fighter threat still demand close-in defences.
segments.body: A real space engagement might be fought at extreme range, much like modern naval missile warfare in which weapons are launched long before impact. Deadlock compresses the action into a confined game space, so its tactical rules need to be judged on their own terms. Fighters remain important within those rules, which makes close defence a basic requirement. Main guns above and below could provide broad coverage, while close-in anti-fighter systems to port, starboard, and forward would leave friendly fighters to help cover the stern.

evidence.note: He contrasts long-range space combat with the game's close action and calls for broadly distributed anti-fighter weapons.

segments.title: Four Artemis battlestars expose a force-design imbalance
segments.summary: A battle group of Artemis battlestars is powerful because they have all-round fire, but that strength points to a weakness in the rest of the fleet.
segments.body: A battle group built around four Artemis battlestars, with a pair of Manticores filling the remaining capacity, is extremely effective. The battlestars can engage threats from any direction while bringing fighters and missiles. That success exposes a structural weakness in the game's force design. The first ship with genuinely broad combat coverage should not have to be the principal capital unit, since smaller escorts ought to provide credible all-round fire at lower cost and in greater numbers.

evidence.note: He describes fielding four Artemis battlestars and says broad fire coverage should not begin only with the main capital ship.

segments.title: Flak works, but missiles need a safe path through it
segments.summary: The game makes flak a valuable fighter defence, while raising a practical question about routing friendly missiles through a ship's own barrage.
segments.body: The flak system resembles the area defence expected against attacking aircraft or fighters. The game rule that the barrage also destroys friendly missiles creates a deconfliction problem. Because the missiles are long-ranged, fire control should be able to time their launch or route them above, below, or around the active flak zone. The mechanic illustrates the need to coordinate defensive fire with a fleet's own outgoing weapons.

evidence.note: He praises flak's battlefield role and argues that missile flight paths could be deconflicted from it.

segments.title: Boarding threats and combat air patrol
segments.summary: Expected Cylon boarding attacks remain manageable when battlestars keep fighter squadrons close for combat air patrol.
segments.body: Cylon boarding parties should be unusually dangerous because machine attackers are less constrained by casualties. In this campaign they have concentrated on battlestars protected by nearby fighters, which makes their attacks easier to defeat. Direct control allows two fighter groups to maintain combat air patrol over four mutually supporting battlestars. That arrangement keeps a coherent local defence while freeing ten of the force's twelve squadrons for interception or offensive work.

evidence.note: He discusses Cylon boarding expectations and describes using two fighter squadrons as close combat air patrol for four battlestars.

segments.title: Viper tactics exploit gaps in ship defence
segments.summary: Vipers are inconsistent in the game, but their flanking and rear attacks underline the cost of leaving gaps in a warship's defensive arcs.
segments.body: The game makes Vipers erratic: they can overwhelm a target or accomplish little unless watched closely. Their best attacks come when they deliberately approach a flank or the stern. Those maneuvers exploit the same defensive gaps found in Colonial warships, while equivalent omissions in Cylon designs seem especially strange for an artificial intelligence facing a fighter-heavy enemy. An advanced force needs layered, all-round defence instead of assuming that an attacker will approach its strongest guns.

evidence.note: He describes Vipers' occasional flanking and rear attacks and links their success to gaps in Cylon and Colonial gun coverage.

segments.title: Carrier choices and the Adamant frigate's limitations
segments.summary: The Adamant depends heavily on its fighter squadron, while a battlestar offers the all-round fighting value that makes a separate carrier hard to justify.
segments.body: A dedicated carrier is hard to justify beside a battlestar when the capital ship is the only genuinely versatile combatant available. A cheaper carrier could make sense in principle, but the game's limited fleet capacity makes every slot compete directly for combat value. Much of the Adamant's utility comes from the single fighter squadron it brings, while its own forward and rear firepower remains weak. A hangar is valuable, but it does not excuse neglecting the basic defensive arcs of the hull carrying it.

evidence.note: He contrasts carriers with battlestars and revisits the Adamant's dependence on fighters and weak gun coverage.

segments.title: A small gun-placement change could transform the Manticore
segments.summary: Moving the Manticore's lower gun aft could open its firing arc without obstructing the missile bays, showing how a modest layout change can reshape combat value.
segments.body: The visible Manticore model places its forward gun on the underside of the hull. The hull blocks much of the mount's aft fire, even though the missile launchers appear farther back underneath the ship. Shifting the gun roughly a third of the hull length aft could preserve missile clearance while opening a much broader field of fire. A small rearrangement, rather than a larger or more expensive weapons fit, could turn a vulnerable sector into near-all-round coverage.

evidence.note: He inspects the Manticore model and explains how moving its lower forward gun aft could clear the missile bays and widen its firing arc.

segments.title: Battlestars should not be the only all-round combatants
segments.summary: A balanced fleet should not need to field only battlestars to achieve dependable all-round firepower.
segments.body: The battlestar is the game's one consistently capable all-round combatant. Requiring a fleet of capital ships to obtain dependable fields of fire is enjoyable in play but unbalanced as force design. A credible navy needs useful combat coverage at more than one size and cost level instead of a single expensive answer to every tactical problem. This remains an early judgment after 32.9 hours with the game, and later ships or more experience could change the assessment.

evidence.note: He concludes that battlestars should not be the only ships with dependable all-round firepower and identifies 32.9 hours of play as the basis for this early judgment.
